newsitem.title: USA: California counties refile tobacco lawsuit.
newsitem.headline: California counties refile tobacco lawsuit.

text.p: A dozen California counties, including San Francisco, refiled their federal lawsuit against the tobacco industry on Monday, one month after a judge dismissed the complaint.
Attorney Robert Nelson, who represents the counties in the case, said the amended lawsuit was filed in U.S. District Court in Oakland, Calif.
In February, a federal judge dismissed the lawsuit, but ruled that the plaintiffs' lawyers could refile an amended complaint by March 31.
"The judge in the last opinion was every explicit about what we needed to proceed," deputy San Francisco attorney Andrew Cheng said. "We believe we've responded to the judge's road map."
The suit aims to recoup health care costs of smokers, to block the tobacco companies from allegedly targeting minors and to force them to disclose nicotine and other research.
The plaintiffs alleged that the tobacco companies engaged in a conspiracy to mislead smokers about the harms of smoking and the addictive nature of nicotine.

In his February ruling, U.S. District Judge D. Lowell Jensen wrote that for the plaintiffs to recover money spent on health care for individual smokers, they would have to prove that each of those injuries were actually caused by smoking.
Jensen also found that the racketeering claims should be dismissed because of the remote nature of the plaintiffs' injuries.
Cheng said plaintiffs would address the judge's concerns about injuries at a later phase in the case.

In response to the ruling, Cheng said the amended complaint now emphasized state fraud and breach of special duty claims. The amended suit preserves the federal racketeering claims for appeal, he said.
"The emphasis is on the fraud and special duty claim," Cheng said. "We're very confident that the judge will look favorably on our approach."
These same California counties have already sued the tobacco companies in state court.

Last week, their attorneys said they would also join a suit against R.J. Reynolds Tobacco Co, challenging "Joe Camel" advertising that allegedly targets children. R.J. Reynolds Tobacco is a unit of RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp.

Earlier this month, Liggett Group, owned by Bennett LeBow's Brooke Group Ltd., broke ranks with other tobacco companies by agreeing to settle with 22 state attorneys general who sued the industry to recoup smoking-related Medicaid health care costs.
Attorneys of the California counties said the Liggett settlement would bolster their case.
"It plainly bolsters our allegations and our proof at trial," said Nelson of the San Francisco firm of Lieff, Cabraser, Heimann & Bernstein.
The state of California, the most populous state, with potentially billions of dollars in claims, has so far not sued the tobacco industry.
